images.label: Cattle Field of Vision Diagram
images.description: Diagram illustrating a cow's visual field showing binocular vision in front, wide monocular vision on the sides, and a blind spot directly behind its back.

images.label: Polled cattle
images.description: Photograph of a polled (hornless) black cattle held with a halter.

images.label: Horned cattle
images.description: Photograph of a horned black and white dairy cattle showing curved horns.

images.label: Desbudding using an electric dehorner
images.description: Close-up photograph showing a person performing disbudding on a young calf using an electric dehorner tool.

images.label: Hot iron rod dehorning
images.description: Photograph showing the use of a hot iron rod with rising smoke applied to a calf's horn bud area for dehorning.

facts: A cow's field of vision includes binocular vision directly in front of its head.
A cow's field of vision includes wide monocular vision on both sides of its head.
A cow has a visual blind spot located directly behind it (at its back).
Polled livestock refers to livestock without horns in species that normally have horns.
Some breeds of cattle are naturally polled through selective breeding.
Disbudding and dehorning is performed on horned animals.
Disbudding and dehorning can be performed as early as 1 month of age.
An electric dehorner is an instrument used for disbudding calves.
A hot iron rod can be used to dehorn calves.
Dewlap is introduced as an anatomical term/topic following the section on poll.

questions.question: What term refers to livestock without horns in species that normally possess horns?
Through what process are some breeds of cattle naturally hornless (polled)?
According to the guide, as early as what age can disbudding and dehorning be performed on calves?
Which of the following tools is shown on the page being used specifically for disbudding a calf?
Based on the cattle vision diagram at the top of the page, where is a cow's blind spot located?

options.A: Directly in front of its nose

questions.question: What type of vision does cattle have directly in front of their face according to the visual field diagram?
Which statement accurately describes the vision on the lateral sides of a cow?

options.A: The cow relies on monocular vision on both sides.
options.B: The cow possesses binocular vision extending 360 degrees.
options.D: The lateral areas cannot detect moving objects.
